interest: Afghans saw Japan's Burmese puppets as genuine nationalists.
overview: Thayer's despatch of August 10, 1943 from Kabul: Afghans were impressed by Japanese propaganda on Burma and disliked U.S. broadcasts calling it a 'Quisling Government'.

people.name: Charles W. Thayer
people.role: U.S. Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in Kabul

people.name: Vidkun Quisling
people.role: Norwegian collaborationist leader (eponym alluded to in text)

subfiles.about: Reports on the Afghan Government's favorable reaction to Japanese radio propaganda and the newly established independent Burmese government, while critiquing ineffective American counter-propaganda.
subfiles.from: Charles W. Thayer, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, U.S. Legation, Kabul
subfiles.summary: Thayer reports Afghan officials saw Burma's new leaders as sincere nationalists and were receptive to Japanese propaganda, while U.S. counter-propaganda fell flat.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 263 from Charles W. Thayer on Afghan Reaction to American and Japanese Propaganda in India and Burma
